root_idea.summary: A single root principle denotes what is opposed to dryness: moisture, freshness, and softness.
root_idea.development: The lexical range develops from moisture and the absence of dryness to soft or pliant qualities, fresh vegetation and ripe dates, and causative, figurative, and idiomatic uses. These developments remain form- and headword-specific rather than constituting one meaning for every Quranic form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested nominal form meaning moist or not dry.
Distinct Quran-attested nominal form specifically denoting fresh ripe dates.

senses.definition: Moist, humid, succulent, or sappy; not dry.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, it is used substantivally for what is opposed to dry. This generic form is distinct from رُطَبٌ, the fresh-ripe-date noun.

senses.definition: Fresh ripe dates, before they become dry.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective noun for dates at the fresh-ripe stage; the Quranic usage refers to dates that are freshly ripe and edible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become moist, humid, succulent, soft, tender, fresh, or supple.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic intransitive verb for becoming the opposite of dry; the same range may be applied literally to things and figuratively to a person becoming soft or supple.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become supple or refreshed through repeated use; in an idiom, for the tongue to be enlivened by speaking or mentioning someone, and for the hands to become practiced through handling something useful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Conventional idiomatic expressions, including رَطُبَ لِسَانِي بِذِكْرِكَ and خُذْ مَا رَطُبَتْ بِهِ يَدَاكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak whatever comes to mind, whether correct or mistaken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct speech-related use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a horse or similar animal with fresh fodder or fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used transitively for supplying the animal with رَطْبَة or رُطَب; it may also describe the animal eating what it is given.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To moisten or make something moist, soft, fresh, or pliant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form II use, including moistening cloth or another object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the tongue supple or refreshed through speaking or mentioning someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative construction parallel to the idiomatic use of رَطُبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed people with fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct transitive Form II usage in which the object supplied is رُطَب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For dates to ripen, or for palm trees to come to bear fresh ripe dates; for people to have or abound in such dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of dates reaching the fresh-ripe stage, of palms having such dates, and by extension of people possessing or having an abundance of them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people or land to become amid, possess, or abound in fresh green herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use applied to pasture or vegetation rather than to dates.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, tender, fresh, green, supple, pliant, or flexible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader adjectival branch applied to such things as food, branches, twigs, plumage, and herbage; the object examples do not restrict the meaning to those classes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh or unpreserved produce or provisions that do not keep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use for articles such as fruits, herbs, or leguminous plants that are not stored for preservation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft or supple in a figurative description of a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed figurative use, including descriptions of a soft or femininely supple girl, boy, young man, or man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Supple or refreshed through speaking or repeated mention.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the conventional expression for a tongue becoming supple or refreshed by mentioning someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an insulting figurative use, an unchaste or adulterous woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional reviling expression applied to a woman or girl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, delicate, or easy, said of life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use in the expression عَيْشٌ رَطْبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Softly or gently, of recitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the conventional expression قَرَأَ القُرْآنَ رَطْبًا, it describes reciting without a loud voice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively brilliant, smooth, clear, fresh, fragrant, or fine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymical use: of pearls for their beauty, smooth exterior, and clarity, and of aloes-wood for freshness, fragrance, or fineness rather than literal moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh, juicy, or green herbage and pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for green vegetation, including seasonal pasture, herbs, leguminous plants, shrubs, or trees; dry vegetation is called حَشِيش.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh green fodder, especially trefoil or clover.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a species of fodder while juicy, fresh, or green before drying; secondary reports extend it to a green meadow and to similar fresh produce such as cucumber, melon, or eggplant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also attested as a surname derived from this occupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abounding in fresh or moist vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of land with abundant رُطْب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well of sweet water among wells of salt water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical description of a freshwater well distinguished from surrounding saline wells.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fed with fresh fodder or fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of an animal fed with رَطْبَة or a person fed with رُطَب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft or supple, as a quality present in a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use meaning one possessing softness or suppleness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft or smooth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct adjectival headword for softness or smoothness, not merely an inflectional variant of the Quranic noun.

cautions: The Quran distinguishes رَطْبٌ, the generic moist or not-dry form, from رُطَبٌ, the noun for fresh ripe dates.
